Class Mhs35TftDisplay

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.tft.Mhs35TftDisplay
All Implemented Interfaces:
Display, TouchScreen
public final class Mhs35TftDisplay extends Object implements Display, TouchScreen
Driver for the MHS-3.5-inch Raspberry Pi display: a 480x320 TFT on the Pi's 40-pin header with an ILI9486 controller and a resistive XPT2046 touch panel. The controller sits behind an SPI-to-parallel bridge, so every command, parameter and pixel is a 16-bit word on the SPI bus, and the display cannot be read back. It is a HAT, so the Portenta Hat Carrier's header carries it: PortentaHatCarrier names its data/command, reset and chip-select pins, and the SPI bus is MCU.getSpi().

Create one instance at startup and pass it to every class that draws. The display starts in LANDSCAPE, 480 pixels wide. A program laid out for a smaller screen, such as the 320x240 of a 2.8-inch panel, calls fitLogicalSize(int, int) once: it keeps drawing in its own coordinates, which the display scales up uniformly to fill the panel, centered, and its touches arrive in those coordinates too.

Pixels are 16-bit RGB565, sent most significant byte first. A full-screen fill sends 307200 bytes, so it takes a noticeable fraction of a second at the core's default SPI clock; small rectangles and text are quick.

The backlight is not switched by this driver: the MHS board's backlight line is not on a pin Juno names, so the panel stays lit whenever the board has power.

  • Method Details

    • setRotation

      public void setRotation(int value)
      Selects PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE, draws at the panel's own resolution again, and restores that rotation's default touch calibration. The existing screen contents are not redrawn.

    • fitLogicalSize

      public void fitLogicalSize(int logicalWidth, int logicalHeight)
      Lets a program laid out for a logicalWidth x logicalHeight screen fill this one: from now on it draws, prints and reads touches in those coordinates, scaled up uniformly as far as the panel allows and centered, and width()/height() return them. The bars beside a scaled area are cleared to black. setRotation(int) returns to the panel's own resolution.

    • beginPixels

      public boolean beginPixels(int x, int y, int w, int h)
      Opens a wxh window with its top-left corner at (x, y) for streaming pixels with pushPixel(int), row by row from the top-left: the fast way to draw a custom bitmap, or a row whose pixels differ, in one pass with no flicker. Returns false, opening nothing, unless the window lies entirely on screen and the display draws at the panel's own resolution (no fitLogicalSize(int, int)). Push exactly w * h pixels before any other drawing call; the last one ends the stream.

    • pushPixel

      public void pushPixel(int color)
